items.item: This topic has a real hands-on lab (lab/mf_shop/, examples.py), unlike most of this chapter's other recent topics: MetricFlow was installed in a separate Python virtualenv (dbt-metricflow is not part of this repo's own environment, and a setuptools<70 pin was needed to work around a build failure — documented in lab/README.md), a dbt project was built over the shop's own star schema, and `mf query` was run by hand to compile the same declared metric to two different SQL queries

at.step: Reveal: the lab — two compiled queries from one declaration

items.item: Both compiled queries' numeric results are cross-checked in examples.py against an independently written plain-SQL aggregate (total revenue, and January's own revenue), not merely assumed correct because MetricFlow produced them

at.step: Reveal: the lab — two compiled queries from one declaration

items.item: The first predict (step 3) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that one metric declaration is permanently tied to whatever grain it was first written for; the reveal at steps 4-5 directly refutes this by executing the identical declaration at two different grains with different results

at.step: Predict: does a metric defined once only ever compile to one fixed query?

items.item: The second predict (step 6) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that MetricFlow could infer a join from matching column names; the reveal at step 7 quotes MetricFlow's own definition of entities as explicitly declared join keys, and the lab's own build is the proof — the automatic join only happened because `product` was declared as an entity on fact_orders

at.step: Predict: does declaring the join key matter, or could it just guess from column names?

items.item: The third predict (step 9) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that any column holding a date should work directly for time-based grouping; the reveal at step 10 is backed by an actual build failure hit while constructing this lab (dbt parse refused to run with the exact error "the semantic layer requires a time spine model... but none was found" until one was added), not just the documentation's own claim
